description: Coverage map for the Enforcement Canary. Every Cedar `forbid` control (@id) MUST appear here with EITHER a `corpus` entry (a Tier-1 decoy probe that proves it fires) OR an `exempt` reason. The coverage-guard test fails CI if any forbid is undeclared, if a mapping points at a missing or exempt corpus entry, or if an exemption has no reason — so the corpus can never silently fall behind the policy set. Extend `surface` beyond cedar-forbid (YAML BLOCK, gh-policy tiers, standalone hooks) as those get enumerated.

exemptReasons.taint-conditioned: Fires only when session taint/trajectory is already elevated; a fresh SessionStart canary has none. Covered by the Cedar policy validator, which stages the required context, and by a future Tier-2 real-attempt canary with staged taint.
exemptReasons.taint-pollution: A Tier-1 decoy probe for this control would mutate session taint state (e.g. a decoy .env read escalates to SECRET), tainting the real session at startup. Covered by the Cedar validator. Becomes Tier-1-eligible once the canary's OK_TALON_ENFORCEMENT_CANARY taint-skip lands.
exemptReasons.context-conditioned: Requires non-default context the probe cannot supply at SessionStart (here: webFetchCount >= 1 plus a sensitivity>=3 resource). Staging it would mean faking session context, which proves the validator, not the live control.

knownGaps.description: Controls PAI's canary covers that 0K-Talon does not have YET. Listed so the gap is tracked rather than silently absent — these are NOT exemptions, they are missing controls.
knownGaps.control-plane-self-protection: 0K-Talon's Governor has no control-plane self-protection: writes to the plugin's own hooks/policies/config are not denied, so one Write can disable a layer. PAI closed this (control-plane-policy-write / -hook-write / -security-edit probes). Port the control, then add the three probes here.
knownGaps.fail-closed-degraded-mode: No degraded-mode circuit breaker: if the Governor cannot evaluate policy it does not fail closed. Port alongside control-plane self-protection.
